correctness.rationale: For R=Z⋉M with M finite of exponent n, (a,m) is a zero divisor exactly when gcd(a,n)>1: a common prime divisor annihilates a nonzero prime-order element of M, while gcd(a,n)=1 makes scalar multiplication by a invertible on M. Thus adjacency depends only on whether gcd(a+b,n)>1. Representatives 0,...,p-1 dominate by reduction modulo the least prime p|n. For fewer than p proposed dominators, for each prime q|n there remains a residue class modulo q avoiding all forbidden negatives; CRT combines these choices, and adding multiples of rad(n) makes the new vertex distinct without changing the avoidance. Hence no smaller set dominates. Finally Ann(0,y)=dZ⋉M for y of order d, whereas elements with nonzero integer coordinate have infinite-index annihilator; maximal proper finite-index annihilator ideals are therefore qZ⋉M for primes q|n. The mixed-prime CRT idempotent gives two zero divisors summing to a unit, so the non-ideal-zero-divisor hypothesis is met.
